overview.text: Saki was the pen name of Hector Hugh Munro (1870–1916), an English writer whose short stories made him known for their sharp wit and satire. Many take aim at upper-class English life, mixing clever humor with a sometimes cruel edge. Munro also wrote journalism, political sketches, a history of Russia, and a novel, but short fiction became his best-known work. Collections such as Reginald, The Chronicles of Clovis, and Beasts and Super-Beasts showcase his unconventional characters, fantastic situations, and knack for an unexpected phrase. His literary signature is the combination of polished social comedy with a distinctly biting, unpredictable tone.

key_facts.text: Saki was born Hector Hugh Munro in Akyab, Burma, in 1870, and died in France in 1916.
He first worked as a political satirist and journalist, and later reported from abroad for the Morning Post.
His stories are often set among upper-class English people and use clever, sometimes cruel humor.
Notable story collections include Reginald (1904), The Chronicles of Clovis (1911), and Beasts and Super-Beasts (1914).
His pseudonym, “Saki,” was identified in a 1927 biography as the name of the cupbearer in the Rubáiyát of Omar Khayyám.
